recommendations.text: Finalise and adopt the necessary measures to transpose the 8.1.2. requirements for castration, tail docking and tooth clipping of piglets as laid down in Council Directive 91/630/EEC and 8.1.3. transpose the requirement for adequate lighting for inspections of 8.1.4. farms as laid down in point 3 of the Annex of Council Directive 8.1.5. 98/58/EC into the French version of the Belgian legislation. 8.1.6. 8.1.7. Ensure that the reports to the Commission on inspections carried 8.1.8. out meet all the requirements of article 8 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC, article 7 of Council Directive 91/629/EEC, article 7 of Council Directive 91/630/EEC and Commission Decision 2000/50/EC. The inspections of calf holdings must be representative of the different systems of farming as laid down in article 7 of Council Directive 91/629/EEC. Ensure that calves, which do not have totally healed navels are not transported as required by point 1 of Chapter 1A of the Annex of Council Directive 91/628/EEC. Also ensure that regarding accommodation for calves, bedding is provided for calves less than 2 weeks old, as required by point 10 of the Annex of Council Directive 91/629/EEC. Ensure that effective monitoring of route plans is carried out and that action is taken where the requirements have not been respected. A system should also be developed to monitor the maximum journey time of 8 hours, particularly where the journey is on a basic vehicle and involves time at a market. Ensure that the register maintained at the staging point meets all the requirements of Council Regulation (EC) No. 1255/97. Ensure that markets provide appropriate facilities, in particular to ensure the safe passage of the animals within the market and for the segregation of different categories of animals so as to prevent any unnecessary suffering. Ensure that stunning equipment in slaughterhouses is operated in such a way that it meets all the requirements of point 2 of article 6 and point 3A of chapter II of Annex C of Council Directive 93/119/EEC. Steps should also be taken to address the difficulties reported in slaughtering unfit animals on farm as required by article 12 of chapter III of Council Directive 93/119/EEC. Ensure that, where necessary, corrective and follow-up action is taken when a deficiency is detected and implement a system to ensure the effective application of sanctions. It would also be beneficial if the system of administrative fines, as proposed by the CCA, could be introduced for more minor offences. 21/03/01 - 51074 25 8.2. audits.title: Potato sector

recommendations.text: Only authorise use of R. solanacearum infected lots for animal feed if they have been heat treated as required in the Council Directive 98/57/EC, Annex VI, point 1.

Implement the requirements in Council Directive 93/85/EEC, Article 5, point 1 (b) for designating potato lots as "probably contaminated" with ring rot. This includes lots other than the ring rot infected lot itself on a contaminated place of production (Annex III, point 1, first indent) and, where a clonal link has been demonstrated also lots on other farms produced from the same clonal origin (Annex III, point 1, last indent).

Implement the requirements in Council Directive 93/85/EEC, Article 5, point 1 (c) for demarcating a zone based on the extent of "probable contamination" with ring rot, including, where a clonal link has been demonstrated, farms having produced potatoes from lots of the same clonal origin as the contaminated lots.
Strictly enforce the requirements in Council Directive 93/85/EEC, Annex IV for disinfection and control of volunteer plants on places of production designated as contaminated with ring rot.
Consider establishing a written contingency plan describing in detail a procedure for handling outbreaks of brown rot and ring rot to ensure uniform and rational action in all cases.

Consider intensifying the survey activity for R. solanacearum in seed potatoes, e.g. so that all basic seed lots are covered. Belgium is requested to report to the Commission 2 months after receiving the final report on action taken on the above points and to submit an action plan indicating the further steps envisaged and by when those will be implemented. *** 24 11. ADDENDUM The Belgian authorities have responded to the recommendations in the mission report. (See the separate document with the Belgian comments on the report for the full text of the response ­ please note that the first recommendation referred to in this response has been removed in the final report). Belgium will follow the first four recommendations and rectify the mentioned non- compliances with the brown rot and ring rot control directives. Preparation of a contingency plan as recommended under (5) will be taken up by the "Crisis Committee" for phytosanitary matters. 25

audits.title: Fishery products, live bivalve molluscs, fish health

recommendations.text: The IVK/IEV has sent an official letter to all veterinarians in charge of controls and inspections in the fisheries sector. They were informed of the shortcomings observed during the FVO mission, with specific emphasis on: - the identification of the fishery products; - the follow up of the corrective actions. The letter was discussed with the Heads of Region (Kringhoofden) on 10 April 2001. A copy of the official letter was attached to the comments.

A "flash action" (flitsactie/coup de sonde) was organised in week 27 focusing on the "identification of fishery products". The IVK/IEV at central level will organise a specific action to evaluate the results of the flash action. The official letter with the announcement of the flash action was discussed with the Heads of Region (Kringhoofden) on 26 June 2001. A copy of the official letter was attached to the comments.

The deficiencies observed during the mission were reported in writing to the establishments involved, the fish auction and the fishing vessels. A copy was sent to the local inspection service for the follow up. The operators, in co-operation with the responsible veterinarian, have to report the kind of corrective actions and the date of their implementation to the IVK/IEV at central level. The veterinarian responsible for the establishment informs the IVK/IEV at central level on the actual follow up of the corrective actions. The labels with the approval number of a French establishment were confiscated by the veterinarian responsible for the establishment and the whole stock of labels was checked.

An official letter was sent to the shipowners of the fishing vessels to ask their attention for the importance of good hygiene and maintenance on board of the vessels. A copy of the official letter was attached to the comments. 26

All veterinarians that are responsible for the supervision and checks in the fishery sector were officially informed in writing on the sampling and analyses on marine biotoxins. The official letter asked for: - samples to be sent the laboratory, without any delay, at the day of sampling except on Friday. Samples taken on Friday are frozen and sent to the laboratory on Monday. - to fill up the request for analysis correctly and not to include additional information concerning the origin the samples on the request form. A copy of the official letter was attached to the comments.

Corrective actions were carried out in the laboratories as a result of the inspection mission: - laboratory for marine biotoxins: * When information concerning the origin of the samples is mentioned on the request form for the analysis, this has to be made illegible by the receptionist before the form is given to the laboratory staff. * Positive results will immediately be faxed to the veterinarian who has sent the sample, the Head of the region and the IVK/IEV at central level. The official report follows by normal mail. - laboratory for heavy metals: * Standards of heavy metals that passed the expiry date were immediately removed and replaced by new standards. * SOP's will be drafted for all official methods and be used in accordance with the instructions of the quality system. - laboratory for microbiology in live bivalve molluscs: * The laboratory has confirmed in writing that all positive results will immediately be reported to the IVK/IEV, both for analyses requested by the IVK/IEV and analyses requested by the dispatch centre. * The MPN test will in the case of doubt (< 10 volume % gas formation) be further analysed. * The analysis starts on the day of arrival of the sample (the date of arrival and the date of the start of the analysis are mentioned in the report). **************** 27

To ensure that there is an official authority to co-ordinate the different services responsible for the supervision and control of traceability and labelling of bovine meat through the whole food chain.
To take urgent measures to enforce the recording of animal movements to/from traders, as well to improve notification to the database of animal movements to slaughter.

To improve the operation of the animal database in order to allow easier access to its information.
To take the necessary measures to ensure that a proper system of registration is in place throughout the food processing chain, included retail outlets.
To improve the operation of, and checks on, meat labelling systems, such that trace-back to holding of origin can be reliably achieved.

To take urgent measures in the unacceptable cutting plant/ distribution centre, and to present those measures to the Commission services within one month of the reception of the draft report. If their response is found to be unsatisfactory, to consider further action in order to ensure consumer health protection. 9. ADDENDUM In their response to the draft report, the Belgian authorities provided additional information on the actions taken in response to the mission. In particular, they noted that: ­ additional guidance had been/was being provided on the application of legislation (section 6.1) ­ the rules governing the coordination and supervision of the different competent authorities were being clarified (section 6.2) 18 ­ a working group on the traceability of bovine meat had been established (section 6.2) ­ a new cattle passport was in preparation, which would record all holdings through which animals had passed. The inclusion of collecting centres and dealers is under discussion (section 6.3) ­ additional controls over dealers and transporters will be imposed from 1 July 2002 (section 6.3) ­ a clarification note has been prepared in respect of the problems seen in beef production and processing establishments. Most of the specific failings had already been resolved. In addition, the following details on action taken in response to specific recommendations were given: Recommendation 8.1.4. Computerised systems for the maintenance of registers by dealers and transporters will come into operation on 1 July 2002. Simplified models of paper-based registers will be prepared and issued under an arrêté ministèriel. The extension of Beltrace, due by the end of 2002, will greatly improve the transmission of data from abattoirs to the central database. Recommendation 8.1.5. Additional clarification on this point was provided. Recommendation 8.1.6. Access to the animal database requires a written request to ACSA, which is responsible for performing the search. Recommendation 8.1.9. Immediate action was taken in this establishment. A "procès verbal" was issued, and solutions are in hand. The Belgian authorities rejected any suggestion following from recommendation 8.2.2 that a health risk to consumers existed from the deficiencies identified during the mission. 19

audits.title: Animal welfare during transport and at the time of slaughter

recommendations.text: The CCA should ensure that all offices are operating a system to ensure that route plans are returned (Article 5(d)(ii) of Council Directive 91/628, as amended). Sanctions imposed on transporters who continue to fail to respect this requirement or who persistently fill in route plans incorrectly should be enforced on a national basis.

The CCA should put in place a system to ensure that all animals are accompanied by documentation, which indicates the date and time of departure (Article 4 of Council Directive 91/628, as amended). This should allow monitoring of journey times, particularly where the journey is on a basic vehicle and involves time at a market.

The CA should revise its instructions on emergency slaughter to ensure that Article 12 of Council Directive 93/119 EEC is fully complied with, particularly regarding the transport of animals with broken legs.

The CA should ensure that vehicles used to transport bovine animals, which are not led individually off the vehicles, should have unloading ramps equipped with adequate lateral protection (point 4 of Annex IA of Council Directive 91/628 as amended). In particular, attention should be given to this requirement when individual vehicle licences are approved.
Checks of vehicles used for long distance transport should ensure that there is direct access at all times to all of the animals (point 3 of the

audits.title: Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies(TSE)

recommendations.text: To review the current "tolerance level" and to ensure that all positive cases are followed up to establish their cause.

To review the current system of feedban controls with a view to ensuring a more targeted approach, and a wider scope of the evaluation of controls carried out at central level in order to ensure that controls meet the targets of the programme, are carried out as required, and to allow corrective action where necessary.

To continue, as a matter of urgency, investigations concerning the high proportion of BAB-cases in order to identify possible causes and take appropriate action. 8.3. With regard to SRM: 1. In the light of the adoption of the modified convention, to accelerate the adoption of implementing measures to provide the responsible authorities with the necessary tools to carry out their duties. Similarly, the regional authorities should accelerate the process of adoption of the measures necessary to give effect to the convention. 2. To urgently review the resources available for SRM controls and to explore all possibilities for a better co-ordination of control activities and co-operation of the services involved. 3. To continue the carrying out of audits, and to ensure that proper follow-up is given to these at all levels.

To provide for improved instructions on the controls to be carried out and to extend the use of standardised control protocols and reports, with a view to facilitating evaluation of the results and follow-up. 23 ADDENDUM Response of the competent authorities to the recommendations Comments from the Belgian competent authorities on the draft report were received on 18 September 2002, and included an outline of the actions planned and/or undertaken to address the recommendations contained in the report. These may be summarised as follows: · Epidemio-Surveillance 1. regular cross-checks: the veterinary services are testing/setting up different methods to speed up and align the data in the databases, one of which requires involvement and agreement of various bodies before it can be tried out. Once the results are known, the new measures emanating from it should ensure concordance between the databases and allow effective cross-checks. 2. procedures concerning rapid tests: the official procedure for confirmation of initially positive results has been adapted to bring it in line with the procedure of the test manufacturer. 3. sampling of small ruminants: experts will be informed of the parameters on which they must base their choice if, locally, they should be faced with needing to select animals from within a large batch. 4. requirements in relation to small ruminant identification and registration: As a first step, the holding register template will be revised to make it easier to use and to bring out more clearly the link between the items of information which it must contain (old number ­ re-tagging number). Following this, it is intended to review the Royal Decree on the identification of small ruminants, in the light of the future decisions adopted at European level. · Feed ban 1. "tolerance level": the text in the control programme will be modified to replace 'tolerance' with 'detection limit' to emphasise that no tolerance level exists. 2. system of feedban controls: the recommendations will be taken into account when drawing up the 2003 control programme, during which that it will also re- examine the advisability of leaving the selection of companies with officials in charge in the Regions (see also footnote 20) . 3. investigations of BAB-cases: these will continue; .to assist in this process, a database is being set up to help identify links and possible causes. · Specified Risk Material 1.-4. All recommendations made are being taken into consideration in the Convention on animal waste which is being drafted, and in regulations and service instructions. In addition, the three Regional CA all provide an indication of actions undertaken or planned. Additional actions already undertaken or announced in relation to specific observations made in the report are indicated in footnotes to the relevant sections in the report. ____________________ 24

audits.title: Eggs and egg products

recommendations.text: Competent authorities I. Training CCA should ensure that inspectors in particular in egg packing centres are trained to control the implementation of the Community requirements for what concerns eggs and egg products identification and grading deadlines for eggs. CA should also satisfy itself that inspectors have an adequate knowledge of pasteurizers and other technical equipment in the establishments. II. Laboratory services CCA should ensure that inspectors in charge of carrying out official sampling have detailed instructions on how to perform the sampling.

Food safety controls - food of animal origin I. Official supervision of egg packing centres, egg-product establishments or establishments using eggs or egg-products as raw material CCA should ensure that instructions are given to the inspectors to standardise and improve the reporting on control activities, especially for what concerns own check controls. II. Trade in eggs and egg products ­ Trade ­ Traceability ­ Export and certification CA should ensure that Community rules on identification of eggs and of products in general (eggs for food industry/egg product establishments, eggs to be downgraded, egg products not fit for human consumption) in egg packing centres as well as the deadlines for the grading of eggs are correctly implemented in the establishments. The CCAs should inform the Commission of the progress and results of the measures taken, within two months following the reception of the final report, including a timetable for completion by a reasonable deadline of measures and actions still outstanding. 8.2. To the Commission Services None 13 9. ADDENDUM TO THE MISSION REPORT DG SANCO/8585/2002 Central competent authority's response to the recommendations in the report The CCA of Belgium already transmitted to the FVO in their communication of 1 April 2003 an action plan addressing all the report recommendations with a timetable for its implementation. This action plan could be summarised as follows: To recommendation 8.1.1: training During the second quarter of 2003, inspectors will receive training concerning the identification and the delay for the classification and the labeling of the eggs. During the same period training will be provided to inspectors in order to strengthen their capabilities of assessing the functioning of pasteurizers. Inspectors will also be instructed to strictly apply the rules on control of egg products. To recommendation 8.1.1: laboratory services Rules for testing have been improved to ensure appropriate tests dependent on the egg product type. To recommendation 8.1.2: food safety controls - food of animal origin Only one service in future will be responsible for controls in packing centers, so that the standardization of inspections will be enhanced. A new instruction relating to the control in packing centers, envisages the checking of own-checks, in particular with regard to the record keeping and the respect of the date of minimum durability. As far as egg product establishments are concerned the inspection form will be improved in order to make compulsory the reporting of all the items checked during an inspection visit. A report form will be established to record a synthetic evaluation of the HACCP when checked in establishments. To recommendation 8.1.2 Trade in eggs and egg products - Traceability - Export and certification A record keeping system will be made compulsory in packing stations that will allow to control in particular the date of minimum durability of eggs. The new standard form of inspection report for packing centers will allow for the control of the denaturation and of the destination of industrial eggs. Furthermore, the respect of the legal provisions with regard to labeling of the eggs will constitute henceforth the condition for the maintenance of the approval of the packing station.

audits.title: Border Inspection Posts

recommendations.text: The CA should take measures to ensure full transposition of Council Directive 97/78/EC.

The CA should, within one month of receipt of the translated final report, submit an action plan which provides adequate guarantees that the shortcomings identified in this report in relation to the proposed BIP at Oostende Port are satisfactorily addressed. 8.2. To the Commission Services It is recommended to the Commission Services to consider the approval of the proposed BIP of Oostende port for HC-T products, only packed with the footnote (2) for temperature controlled products fit for human consumption, if satisfactory guarantees in relation to the correction of the deficiencies found, are received from the Belgian Competent Authority. 10 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/8737/2002 Competent authority response to the recommendations and conclusions in the report 8.1.1 and 6.1. : The CCA stated that they would renew their efforts towards the legislative services to implement all elements of Council Directive 97/78/EC. The CCA stated that the instruction for the implementation of veterinary fees on milk products would be in force shortly. The CCA will carry out the next audits to the BIPs in February/March 2003. 6.2. Veterinary organisation: The CCA stated that the training of the responsible staff would be continued in several practical sessions at other BIPs. In addition the responsible veterinarian of the port BIP will start controls under the supervision of a veterinarian from the BIP Oostende airport. 6.3. Facilities: The loading bays have been closed. The CCA will verify all aspects of the customs designated area status of the BIP with the customs services. 6.4. Equipment: Containers for the transportation of samples will be delivered and the sampling equipment and the fridge/freezer will be placed in the inspection room. The harbour authority orders an unloading tool. 6.5. Hygiene: The cleaning program will be adapted and the dispenser has been put in place. The water supply will be improved, including warm water. 6.6. Documentation and records: The basic legislation for other products will be put in place, as the CCA was not informed about the larger range of the imports. The records will be adapted as mentioned in the report. 6.7. Identification, selection and notification of consignments: The prenotification form will be adapted. The veterinary services and the customs authorities will examine possibilities to improve the procedure. 6.8. Procedure for veterinary checks, decision on consignments, transit, transhipment: The Annex B will be adapted and the transit procedure will be clarified. 6.9. Kitchen waste: The staff of the BIP will have the co-ordinates of the responsible service at its disposal. 11

audits.title: Animal nutrition

recommendations.text: To continue the effort to enhance co-operation and co-ordination amongst central authorities, regional services and Customs involved in official feed controls.
To ensure that the maximum limit fixed in the EU legislation for some additives in compound feedingstuffs is respected.
To ensure the proper documentary check and physical check of feed materials traded and used in the country.
To ensure a uniform approach with regard to the criteria used for the organisation and implementation of official inspections in the different provinces.
To ensure that all products imported from third countries are controlled in compliance with Chapter II of Council Directive 95/53/EC at the point of entry.
To ensure that intermediaries are approved for all the activity they perform.

To ensure that existing procedures for dealing with non-compliances in approved and registered establishments and intermediaries, are uniformly applied. ______________________ 18 ADDENDUM Belgian competent authority's response to the recommendations in the report In their response to the draft report of 13 August 2003, the Belgian competent authorities announced the following actions in relation to recommendations made in the report: 1. In order to reinforce controls on feed imported from third countries, contact will be made with the Customs and Excise Administration for implementing of the existing protocol. 2. In order to ensure proper implementation of the new legislation relating to the labelling of compound feed (open declaration), checks on documents accompanying feed materials will be stepped up in 2004. Furthermore greater use will be made of check-list for checking the labelling of feed materials in order to standardise and intensify documentary checks. 3. The AFSCA's "Crisis prevention and management" Service is currently preparing a contingency plan for the whole of the food chain. 4. The directors of the two "Implementation and Coordination Units" (UNIC), one for the Flemish-speaking and the other for the French and German-speaking parts of the country, will be assisted by teams which will ensure by means of audits that the Directorate-General for Control's instructions are being followed. The CA will also be responsible for general supervision (by service). In addition, a database and an integrated control system (SCI) are being developed and will receive all the data associated with inspections. The DGs for Control Policy and Controls will establish criteria in the control programmes and control plans, mainly in the form of recommendations, in order to harmonise the organisation of inspections. 5. Existing lists of representatives of foreign establishments will be sent to Provincial Control Units (UPCs), border inspection posts and customs offices. 6. The control programme and control plans for 2004 will draw attention to inspection of the activities performed by establishments.

audits.title: Import Controls

recommendations.text: Both the Belgium Federal Agency for the Safety of the Food Chain, and the Customs Service should ensure that up to date information on Commission Decisions are disseminated to provincial level in a timely manner.

The Competent Authority should ensure that Provincial Control Units are adequately resourced to carry out their official control functions with the meaning of Council Directive 89/397/EC, Art 4. 1a and 3.

The Belgium Federal Agency for the Safety of the Food Chain and the Federal Customs Service should agree on a formal basis for co- ordinating their responsibilities concerning import control of foodstuffs of plant origin.

Taking account of the importance of Antwerp as an import point into the Community, the Competent Authorities should implement a system of prioritisation of import controls based on comparative risk assessment for foodstuffs of plant origin. 29

The Competent Authorities should widen the scope of official control at the point of entry to include foodstuffs of known risks, e.g. RASFF alerts associated with foodstuffs, other than those for which Commission Decisions apply such as 3-MCPD in soya sauce, and ochratoxin A in coffee.

The Competent Authority should ensure that all health certificates comply with requirements of Commission Decisions, in particular health certificates for consignments of peanuts originating from China.

The Competent Authority should ensure that adequate sampling equipment is made available to officials carrying out sampling so as to permit a more representative sampling of consignments, and take steps to harmonise sampling procedures between Provincial Control Units.
The Competent Authority should ensure that time for sampling and analysis respects the 10-day maximum period for release of consignments following sampling and analysis.

The Competent Authority should ensure that officials evaluate the implementation of the requirement that food operators implement food safety systems based on certain HACCP principles as required by Art 8.2 of Council Directive 93/43/EEC. Written assurances should be forwarded to the European Commission with regard to all of the above recommendations within two months of receipt of the final translated mission report. The Competent Authority should provide detailed information on the actions that will be taken and propose deadlines by which these actions will be completed. 30 ADDENDUM In their response to the draft report, the competent authorities have addressed most of the recommendations as follows: Point 1 The Belgium authorities indicated in their response that a procedure has been developed for the dissemination of information from the FASFC. The relevant messages will be drafted by the Control Policy Administration and disseminated to the Control and Laboratories Administrations and other interested parties (where relevant). With regard to Commission Decisions 2002/679/EC and 2002/678/EG, the Control Policy Administration has drafted a new memorandum. The Customs Service will draw up new procedures, which they expect to validate towards the end of November 2003. Point 2 The FASFC is currently undergoing integration and restructuring process. Part of this integration process is the performance of a "resizing exercise" in the local Provincial Control Units (PCUs). The result of this "resizing" may be the redeployment of staff to provinces where there is a staff shortage. This process will be starting very shortly, as the local PCU Heads were appointed by the Minister on 17 October 2003, and will be concluded in February 2004. Point3 A co-operation agreement (protocol) will be drawn up between the FASFC and the Customs Service. This protocol will govern the practical agreements between these two organisations, and will be finalised towards the end of this year. A request to draft a basic text of the protocol has already been sent to the Customs Service. Point 4 At the beginning of 2003, a specific "Control programme" cell was created within the Control Policy Administration. The main task of this cell is to evaluate the results of the analyses and audits using a scientifically supported programme, which will be fully operational in the second half of 2004. Point 6 The field services will pay extra attention to the presence of the health certificate from now on, within the meaning of Decision 2002/79/EG. Point 7 The Control Administration and the field services have undertaken to obtain sampling equipment (including sampling sticks +/- 2 m in length) for taking five individual samples per sampling occasion. The aim is to have achieved this by the end of 2003. 31 Point 8 The Laboratory Administration will be instructed by the Control Policy Administration about the maximum periods to be respected, and the laboratory in question will be contacted in order to remind it of the deadline. Point 9 A revision of the audit procedures in question is under way. A draft version is already available. The frequency of the audits (depending on whether there is a quality system in place, the company history, its size, etc.) is currently being discussed in the "Audit procedures" working group. 32

audits.title: Plant protection products and residues in foodstuffs of plant origin

recommendations.text: Commission Directive 2002/63/EC on methods of sampling for the official control of pesticides analysis should be transposed without further delay.
For formulation analyses of plant protection products, the samples should be adequately homogenised.
Regional inspectors should have access to data on previous inspections in order to plan their work appropriately.

When developing structures of the Food Agency, the competent authority should take appropriate measures to ensure that adequate communication and co-operation is established between the three services for controls of marketing and use, for pre-harvest inspections and for pesticide residues, at both central and regional level.

Analytical uncertainty, based on data on accuracy and precision of residue analyses should be taken into account for confirmation of non-compliance, as 22 required under Commission Directive 2002/63/EC, and also in connection with risk assessments regarding non-compliant samples.

Continue with validation and accreditation of methods for more pesticides covered by EU MRL legislation, and it should be ensured that the quantification limits meet the requirements of EU MRL legislation.

In the residue analysis, all positive results should be confirmed at least with a second column, and ensured by adequate calibration. An action plan in response to the recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission within 2 months of dispatch of the final translated report. This action plan should clearly set out the manner and deadline by which the competent authorities will address each recommendation.
ADDENDUM The Belgian Competent Authorities submitted an initial action plan in response to the recommendations in their response to the draft report. 23

audits.title: Traceability of Beef and Beef products

recommendations.text: Take the action necessary to ensure that the draft royal decrees which were presented are implemented quickly, particularly those concerning the labelling of beef and beef products and those relating to the electronic transmission of data on slaughter operations by abattoirs

Put in place a plan for checking the labelling and traceability of beef and beef products at national level in order to ensure that the regulatory provisions in this area are implemented effectively and correctly at all levels of the food chain.

Put in place new training measures for officials required to carry out checks on the labelling and traceability of beef and beef products; in particular, these measures should stress those aspects of the work relating to registration and commercial documents.
Take urgent action to ensure that the movement of animals is registered and notified by wholesalers, and to improve the declaration via the website of the movement of animals sent for slaughter.

Take the action necessary to ensure that beef from bovines imported into Belgium before 1996 is labelled properly. An action plan, indicating the measures taken or planned in order to take account of the conclusions and recommendations of the present report, accompanied by the timetable for their implementation, should be sent to the Commission no later than two months from the date on which the final report is received. ADDENDUM In their comments on the draft report, the competent authorities in Belgium provided clarification of the action implemented or planned as a result of the mission. This action relates to several of the shortcomings brought to light during the mission and responds to most of the recommendations made in the report. 3

audits.title: Animal welfare

recommendations.text: Transporters draw up and complete route plans as laid down in paragraph (d) of Article 5(A)(2) of Directive 91/628/EEC and demonstrate that steps have been taken to meet the animals' needs for feed and water during the journey as per paragraph (f) of Article 5(A)(2) of Directive 91/628/EEC.
The CA stamping the route plan at the places of departure give notice of its existence through the ANIMO system, as required by paragraph (c) of Article 5(A)(2) of Directive 91/628/EEC.
All species are accompanied throughout their journey by documentation enabling, in particular, to check the date and time of departure, as required by Article 4 of Directive 91/628/EEC.
Suitable facilities are provided at markets so that animals can rest and have access to water, as necessary (second indent of Article 2(2)(e) of Directive 91/628/EEC).
Calves are only transported when considered fit for transport (point 1 of Chapter I(A) of the Annex to Directive 91/628/EEC).

Animals at slaughterhouses, which have not been killed within 12 hours of their arrival, are fed (point 9 of Chapter II of Annex A to Directive 93/119/EC). 9 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)9281/2003 The competent authority did not offer any comments on the draft report. 10

audits.title: Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopaties (TSEs)

recommendations.text: To guarantee that the implementation of the total feed ban includes controls on imported product for animal nutrition other than fishmeal.
To ensure a uniform and risk based approach with regard to the criteria used for the organisation and implementation of official inspections in the different provinces.
To ensure that the expression of the result of microscopic examination is in line with the Annex to Directive 98/88/EC
To ensure that any presence of PAO in feedingstuffs, and impurities in fats which exceed the EU limit of 0,15% are followed by adequate and prompt action.

To continue investigations concerning the high proportion of impurities in ruminant fats in order to identify possible causes and to take appropriate action. ______________________ 7 DG (SANCO)/7040/2004 - MR - Final Addendum Response of the competent authorities to the recommendations Comments from the Belgian CCA on the draft report were received on 21 June 2004, and included an outline of the actions planned and/or undertaken to address certai s contained in the report. These may be summarised as follows: · Control programmes for imported products will be re-evaluated in the context of the feed ban and, if necessary, will be adapted by AFSCA's Directorate-General for Control Policy in order to strengthen controls on raw materials other than fishmeal. · Where appropriate, criteria will be identified so that the establishments inspected are selected in accordance with the risk posed, while the information sheets for the UPCs will be specified by AFSCA's Directorate-General for Controls. · The way in which the result of microscopic examinations is expressed in the system will be re-assessed by AFSCA's Directorate-General for Laboratories in order to comply with the existing guidelines. · As regards the purity of ruminant fats, the Laboratories DG is organising a ring test involving various EU laboratories that use the ISO 663-2000 method, with a view to remedying the wide variability observed in the results. If necessary, the sensitivity and repeatability of the methods used will be re-assessed by the Laboratories DG. The action to be taken when animal protein levels of less than 0.1% are detected or when impurities are found in ruminant fats will be evaluated and specified, in particular as regards sampling (methodology and control plan) and the reasons for the high proportion of impurities in the fats (AFSCA's Control DG). 8

audits.title: Food Hygiene

recommendations.text: The competent authorities should address the resource issues indicated in this report.

The competent authorities should address the issue of communication with the municipal authorities, in particular with regard to the communicating alerts as part of the Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed.
The competent authorities should ensure that official controls cover all aspects of Council Directive 93/43/EEC during inspections, as foreseen in Art 8(1) of that Directive.
The Competent authorities should continue to address the issue of poor implementation of HACCP in those food sectors falling within the scope of this mission.

The competent authorities should ensure that food premises are inspected at a frequency which has regard to the risk associated with the premises as foreseen in Art 8(2) of Council Directive 93/43/EEC. A programme in response to these recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission Services within a period of two months after the dispatch of the final translated report. 21 10. ADDENDUM Regarding the recommendations made in the draft report, the following initial comments were provided in relation to actions that have been or will be take 1 "Part of the problem has already been addressed through the increase in staff: · 20 inspectors and 65 controllers in 2001; · 43 inspectors and 96 controllers in 2004. The process of assigning staff to the PCUs is still under way and will be completed in September-October 2004 with a new increase in staff, particularly in the distribution sector." Once the first guides have been approved by the Agency, self-checking audits in the sectors concerned will be delegated to private inspection organisations. 2004 is the first time that the Agency has worked on an annual control plan. Stepping up and improving control of the execution of this plan, introduced during 2004, will overcome the technical difficulties linked to extracting data from INFANA and will thus provide a clearer picture of the situation in the field. Organisation of the controllers' work will be rationalised by such means as the introduction of transport for samples intended for analysis, to avoid controllers having to take samples to the laboratories themselves. Implementation of the control plan will also be improved through better coordination between sampling visits and inspections. The introduction and use of a central data bank (FOODNET) and the transfer of part of the administrative work to administrative staff should also enable controllers to make more site visits." Recommendation 2 "A coordination meeting is planned in order to establish a memorandum of understanding between FASFC and the municipal inspection services. This will deal with exchanges of the results of analyses and inspections, and the exchange of information relating to the Rapid Alert System, collective food poisoning and coordinated programmes." Recommendation 3 · "Drawing up of vertical checklists and vertical standards · Training of controllers and inspectors in HACCP auditing and the use of horizontal and vertical checklists and vertical standards The horizontal checklist is in three sections: 22 ­ one is for verifying the existence of a policy and of a system for quality management in the undertaking; ­ a second is for ensuring that establishments have prior hygiene measures in place; ­ a third is for monitoring self-checking (based on the seven HACCP principles) in the establishment. · Introduction of vertical checklists and vertical standards." Recommendation 4 "Reinforce self-checking audits in establishments (2005 control programme) Encourage federations to draw up guides to good practice (information campaigns, training, etc.) Introduce a financial incentive for establishments which have introduced an HACCP system." Recommendation 5 "From 2005, the annual inspection and audit plan for establishments will be based on a general assessment of the risks associated with the establishment's activities. In relation to the 2004 control plan, therefore, the distribution of inspections will be different, but the overall rate of inspection cannot increase by more than 10% because of the staff currently available." 23

audits.title: Plant passport

recommendations.text: Article 3 of Commission Directive 92/105/EEC is transposed in its entirety; (2) guidelines concerning the visual checks to be carried out by registered establishments, in accordance with Article 2(d) of Commission Directive 92/90/EEC, must be available, preferably in writing; (3) producers of potatoes for human consumption who sell their produce directly are registered, in accordance with Article 1 of Commission Directive 93/50/EEC; (4) the PP issued in Belgium consists of a label, or of a label with the accompanying document, and that it be physically attached to the regulated articles, as indicated in Article 1(2)(a) and Article 3(1) of Commission Directive 92/105/EEC and in Article 2(1)(f) of Council Directive 2000/29/EC; 4 (5) the registered establishments inform the competent authority about the regulated articles produced or marketed by them so that official checks can be carried out, as provided for in Article 10(1) and (2) of Council Directive 2000/29/EC; (6) host plants which are susceptible to E.a. and which are sent to protected zones between 1 April 2004 and 1 April 2005 comply with the specific requirements listed in the Community legislation in force before 1 April 2004, as stipulated in point 21 of Annex IV, Part B of Council Directive 2000/29/EEC. This means that host plants which are susceptible to E.a. and are grown in buffer zones where an outbreak of E.a. has been officially reported are not sent to protected zones as long as the risk of infection has not been ruled out; (7) the host plants for E.a. which will be marketed in the protected zones after 1 April 2005 comply with the conditions laid down in point 21 of Annex IV, Part B of Council Directive 2000/29/EEC; (8) PPs with the ZP and RP code are issued in accordance with Article 10(3) of Council Directive 2000/29/EC and Article 3 of Commission Directive 92/105/EEC. In particular, regulated articles intended for protected zones must comply with the specific requirements set out in Annex IV, Part B; (9) all the registered establishments which are authorised to issue PPs, including nurseries, are inspected at least once a year, in accordance with Article 6(5) of Council Directive 2000/29/EC; (10) the documentary checks provided for in Article 4 of Commission Directive 92/90/EEC are carried out regularly in registered establishments with due diligence; (11) where irregularities arise, follow-up checks are always carried out, as provided for in Article 1(6) of Commission Directive 92/90/EEC and Article 1(1) of Commission Directive 92/105/EEC. The competent authority in Belgium should consider taking the following steps: (1) ensure more effective coordination of the PP system in all the provinces: - by continuing to revise relevant procedures (work plan, evaluation of work and inspection sheet); - by drawing up a special handbook to assist the inspectors in their work; - by holding meetings and refresher courses on aspects of the PP for inspectors from the various UPCs. (2) strengthen cooperation with and the provision of information to registered establishments in order to improve knowledge and understanding of the PP system. (3) increase the number of occasional checks referred to in Article 12(5) of Council Directive 2000/29/EC. An action plan in response to these recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission within two months of receipt of the final report. This action plan should 5 clearly set out not only the manner in which the competent authorities will address each recommendation but also the corresponding deadlines. Addendum The Belgian authorities made comments on the draft report; these are published separately. They also commented on the recommendations made by the FVO mission team, which are set out in the present report. In response to recommendations (1) and (5), the Belgian authorities explained that, when the Royal Decree of 3 May 1994 was next amended, a correction concerning the use of capital letters would be added to it as well as the requirement that a declaration concerning crops be made when the application for authorisation was submitted and that notification be provided of subsequent amendments every year. In response to recommendation (2), the Belgian authorities explained that technical fact sheets and checklists on the completion of plant health inspections were currently being drawn up for each plant species, for the attention of inspectors and monitoring agents. The intention was to make this information available to producers as well so that they could be in possession of the same information when carrying out visual checks. In response to recommendation (3), the Belgian authorities explained that all producers of potatoes for human consumption would be registered as of 1 January 2005, following the entry into force of the Royal Decree on self-monitoring. In response to recommendation (7), the Belgian authorities explained that the necessary measures had been taken in 2004 with a view to implementing the new provisions on fire blight. These measures were taken from the instructions (PPV 813 of 13.06.2004) concerning fire blight. In response to recommendations (8), (9), (10) and (11), the Belgian authorities explained that these points would be monitored more effectively in future. Finally, the Belgian authorities explained that they would take note of the matters to be addressed and that the necessary training would be provided once all the instructions and checklists had been finalised. 6

audits.title: Residues and contaminants in live animals and animal products, including controls on veterinary medicinal products

recommendations.text: Ensure that Commission Decision 2000/68/EC is implemented without delay. With regard to the NRCP
Update the NRCP with regard to the actual testing carried out and the scope and performance of the individual laboratories involved in testing.
Ensure that the NRCP is presented in a uniform format regarding the numbers of animals and that the summary tables are filled out in accordance with Commission requirements.

Improve communication and coordination between the bodies responsible for the design of the NRCP, the organisation of the sampling and the laboratory network in order to improve the effectiveness of the NRCP and to optimise the use of resources in the laboratories.
Involve the FPS in the planning phase of the NRCP to consider objective information about the usage patterns of VMPs in order to optimise the design of the NRCP. With regard to the laboratories

Improve the performance of the NRL and establish an action plan for the development, validation and accreditation of analytical methods in order that all NRL functions are fulfilled in line with Community legislation.
Ensure that samples are delivered only to laboratories with a scope and performance of testing, which is clearly laid down in the NRCP. With regard to VMPs

Ensure that VMPs containing active substances not listed in Annexes I, II or III to Council Regulation (EEC) No 2377/90 are not used in food producing animals, and remove any such products for food producing animals from the market.

Ensure that for all authorised VMPs containing active substances with MRLs, all necessary drug withdrawal times are indicated. (10 ) In their comments to the draft report the CA stated that the DGMP pointed out at the closing meeting that the FVO only took into account the aspects of consumer health, while the animal health and welfare aspects, which are equally important and closely linked to the availability of VMPs for the treatment of diseases in minor species, were not taken into consideration. 17
Take measures to ensure that pigeons slaughtered for human consumption do not contain residues of VMPs not permitted for use in food producing animals.
Ensure that only medicated premixes with a finalised renewal assessment are on the market.
Ensure that all medicated premixes are clearly identified as such in the national register.
Improve the regular control system for veterinary practices and regulate the mutual competences of the responsible bodies in this field.

Take actions to ensure that treatment records on farm fulfil all requirements of Community legislation. 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 7290/2004 In their letter of 9 March 2005 in response to the draft report, the Belgian CA described a number of actions to be taken to address the deficiencies highlighted in the draft report. In relation to the recommendations above, the response can be summarised as follows: Legislatio 1: with regard to the implementation of Commission Decision 2000/68/EC, a new national regulation is required to be drafted, which will enter into force on 1 October 2005. NRCP: Recommendation 2: the NRCP 2005 will contain updated data relating to the methods used, and in regard to the scope and performance of the involved laboratories. Recommendation 3: the reporting of the NRCP 2005 is based on a web application developed by the European Commission, which will ensure harmonised presentation of the data. Recommendation 4: the CA announced that meetings will be organised with the officials of the NRCP, DG laboratories, the NRL and the laboratories concerned. Besides, an internal procedure is currently in preparation to define more precisely the different stages of the process of scheduling the control plans and the exchanges between the different persons concer 5: the FPS has been officially requested to provide the Agency with particulars on the sale of the different VMPs and a protocol will be prepared to ensure the continuous transmission of these data. Laboratories: Recommendation 6: in order to improve the NRL's performance, an action plan has been prepared, setting out the future objectives. This includes also a detailed timetable of activities scheduled for 2005. Recommendation 7: the CA stated that an evaluation will be made of the laboratories responsible for analyses in the framework of the NRCP as regards 18 requirements concerning scope and performance. Parameters such as accreditation, approval, validation and others will also be taken into consideration. VMPs: Recommendation 8: with regard to the removal of VMPs, containing active substances which are not listed in Annex I, II or III to Council Regulation (EEC) No 2377/90, for food producing animals from the market, the CA had taken action to withdraw 4 products from the market. Recommendation 9: the CA announced several actions which have already been taken. In addition, the Registration Department of the DGMP (veterinary unit) intends to terminate the five-yearly evaluations for renewal of several medicaments by 30 October 2005 (which corresponds to the transposition of the new Directive 2004/28/EC) in order to permit a final five-yearly renewal of an updated dossier after this date. However, it will not be possible to meet this deadline unless supplementary staff are allocated to the u 10: the CA announced that letters concerning withdrawal of marketing authorisation for several products have been prepared for signature by the Minister. In addition, CA will re-evaluate the five-yearly renewal of various products. Recommendation 11: the CA stated that it will not be possible to carry out the evaluation within a reasonable time unless supplementary staff resources are allocated to the veterinary u 12: the list of medicated premixes was updated which will be included in the Commented Catalogue of VMPs 2005 (publication scheduled for September 2005). In the meantime information will be circulated to the pharmacists and veterinarians via a Folia Veterinaria (publication scheduled for the second quarter of 2005). Recommendation 13: a task distribution protocol is currently being prepared which will describe the competencies of the FPS and the Agency concerning the controls carried out on veterinary deposits. Besides, it is envisaged in the personnel plan for 2005 to employ two veterinarians to inspect the deposits. Recommendation 14: the CA stated that the Royal Decree of 14 November 2003 on self-regulation, notification requirements and traceability in the food chain, which entered into force on 1 January 2005, specifies that "stockfarmers must register veterinary medicinal products administered or any other treatment to which the animals were subjected, as well the dates of administration or treatment and the withdrawal periods"; this registration is not limited to any period in the animal's life. ________________

audits.title: Fishery products & bivalve molluscs

recommendations.text: Generalities related to CA FP/LBM control system performance The following documentation should be forwarded to the Commission services as soon as they are available and, if not finalised at the time of providing the comments to the draft report, detailed information should be provided regarding the situation at that time: - the final version of the protocol between VMM and the FASFC, regarding the provisions for the transposition of the phytoplankton monitoring requirements of Council Directive 91/492/EEC; - the updating of the establishments' lists, including the actual delisting by the Ministry of Public Health of the dispatch/purification centre; - the corrective measures of the shortcomings previously identified in establishments by the CA and/or identified by the mission team should be followed up in the establishments visited during the mission and in all other establishments that were not visited but that may have similar shortcomings; - the major deficiencies found during the mission and not previously identified by the CA should be followed up in the establishments visited during the mission and in all other establishments that were not visited but that may have similar shortcomings; - laboratories performing analyses for establishments' own-checks should only use methods that are in accordance with the approval procedures and in particular to the NRL positive list of validated methods.

Live bivalve molluscs Bivalve molluscs, in particular Scallops, should only be placed on the market if they do not contain higher contaminant levels than those specified in Commission Regulation 466/2001/EC. Furthermore, the FASFC should keep 14 the Commission services informed of the results of contaminated Scallops and the measures taken whenever high levels of Cadmium are detected.

Fishery products During production and before they are released for human consumption, fish and FP must be subject to a visual inspection for the purpose of detecting and removing any parasites that are visible in accordance to the requirements of Council Directive 91/493/EEC and Commission Decision 93/140/EEC. Whenever fish is sampled for histamine analysis, the sampling procedure to be followed by the CA should be the one required by Council Directive 91/493/EEC. 15 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/7561/2005 All the recommendations on the report have been addressed by the Belgium CCA's communication to the FVO of 29 July 2005. It included details of corrective actions already undertaken and other planned actions, in particular: - Generalities: actions planned to be implemented during the months of September (e.g. VMM protocol and letter) and October 2005 (e.g. follow-up inspection s to vessels); - Live bivalve molluscs: September 2005 (i.e. use of mice in NRL for marine biotoxins); periodic reporting to the Commission of the heavy metals results of analysis carried out in scallops; - Fishery products: as from 2006, parasite checks will also be mandatory in the retail trade.
